claim: Humans in category learning are not purely rule, prototype or exemplar users. Strategy shifts with task, stage and instructions; no single model family wins across the 30 classic data sets.
agent_test: Label tasks by structure at S0; check that the agent does not apply one strategy to all classes.

claim: Early learning looks prototype-like and later learning looks exemplar-like in humans (Smith and Minda 1998; 14 six-dimension stimuli, blocks of 56). A meta-learned model reproduces the drift (slope -0.01 +/- 0.004, z=-2.54) but a plain meta-learned model does not (z=-0.47). Gap search: Nosofsky (2000) and Vanpaemel & Pattyn (2006) disputed the flexibility of the prototype models in the Smith and Minda 2000 reanalysis (summaries only, not opened).
agent_test: Test whether an agent that summarises early and stores instances late beats a fixed strategy.

claim: Meta-learning a network on LLM-generated category tasks (ERMI) fits human data better than raw prompted Claude-v2: BIC 38722.13 vs 39816.90 (Badham) and 41207.20 vs 42401.42 (Devraj); MSE to human error 0.05 vs 0.18. Re-checked against the paper text. One lab, one paper.
agent_test: Replicate the prompted-participant comparison on a current model.

claim: A prompted LLM (Claude-v2) finds Shepard Type 2 harder than Types 3-5, unlike the classic adult-human order. Gap search: that order (I < IV < III < V < II < VI) is the 'general' order humans show with integral stimuli, children and monkeys, so it is not clearly an LLM anomaly. No frontier-model Shepard run was found.
agent_test: Run the six Shepard types as text tasks on our agent with permuted labels and compare against BOTH the classic and the general human order; report Type II as a distribution over runs.

claim: A Cobweb hierarchical concept model gives human-like Shepard learning curves at the basic level (r=0.981 Type I, 0.929 II, 0.751 III, 0.984 V; Type VI -0.375) and Medin-Schaffer fits (r=0.768 leaf, 0.713 basic). It shows both prototype and exemplar traits.
agent_test: Hierarchical memory with basic and leaf levels for problem-class retrieval; test against flat retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: Pretrained LLMs generalise from in-context examples in an exemplar-like way when small and more rule-like when larger (1B near exact exemplar; 70B more rule-based). Transformers trained from scratch generalise rule-like in weights and exemplar-like in context.
agent_test: Test a rule-writing step vs example-only prompting at matched tokens, by model size.

claim: In-context learning is better with blocked trials for rule-like categories and fails on rotated (non-rule) categories. Llama 2 rule-like blocked 93.91% (601/640), interleaved 82.99% (478/576); rotated 23.59% and 24.48%. GPT-3.5 shows no curriculum effect (p=0.63). Humans: interaction p=0.04, d=0.47 blocking, d=0.33 interleaving. Re-checked.
agent_test: Order few-shot examples blocked vs interleaved by task type; check whether rule-like tasks gain from blocking.

claim: LLMs learn better in context from stated rules than from examples. Instruct-minus-base gap is +0.178 for rules and -0.024 for examples. Rule gain is largest on Operator Function and Set Game (about +0.3 to +0.4) and small on Tapatan, Noun Class Agreement, Lexical Category Inference. Related work (Liu 2024, Davidson 2026) unread. Gap search: Liu 2024 shows the gain needs a correct rule (GPT-4-turbo 30% to 96% with the true rule); their models' self-stated rules did not track their own accuracy (r=0.0013).
agent_test: Add a state-the-rule-first step and compare to few-shot-only at equal tokens on rule-structured classes.

claim: LLM in-context concept learning degrades as Boolean complexity grows: Gemma-2-9B 83% to 66%, Qwen2-72B 90% to 74% across classes 1-5; Pearson r -0.961 to -0.854 (the 72B model only p=0.065). Humans show the same law (Feldman 2000, unread). Gap search: Boolean complexity predicts the classic Shepard order only; an entropy-based measure fits both orders (R2 .829 and .970), and Boolean rank correlation falls on larger structures (about .79 on 4[4]). Use as a soft prior.
agent_test: Use a complexity score at S0 to predict when to spend more tokens; test whether it predicts agent failure.

claim: Bayesian inference over natural-language hypotheses proposed by an LLM matches human few-shot concept learning: Number Game R^2=0.95 (100 samples); logical concepts R^2=0.81, within 3% of human accuracy, better than GPT-4 alone.
agent_test: Test propose-hypotheses-then-score vs direct answer on rule-induction items at equal tokens. Goodman 2008 numbers unread.

claim: Inside LLMs, in-context classification is best matched by a prototype-like online algorithm over final-layer representations; amplifying task-aligned activity does not improve behaviour; more flexible linear learners do better from the same representations.
agent_test: Not testable on a closed-model agent; background only.

claim: LLM representations support prototype and exemplar categorisation: prototype 90.64% with 24 demos (FastText 77.86%, sense vectors 85.13%), 90.87% with 48 demos on THINGSplus; nearest-neighbour exemplar 87.46%. Odd-one-out plateaus at 52.41% vs human ceiling 67.67%. Re-checked.
agent_test: Prototype retrieval (class summary) vs exemplar retrieval (nearest case) for problem classes at equal tokens.

claim: Experience-based agent memory gains are modest and uneven: ExpeL insights-only vs retrieval-only 36% vs 31% (HotpotQA), 50% vs 55% (ALFWorld), 37% vs 38% (WebShop); ERL +7.8 points over ReAct with distilled heuristics while few-shot trajectories fall below baseline. Gap search adds: ReasoningBank WebArena 40.5 none, 42.1 raw trajectories (Synapse), 44.1 workflows (AWM), 48.8 distilled strategies; retrieving 1 experience 49.7, 4 experiences 44.4 (subset). Dynamic Cheatsheet AIME 2024: full history 26.7 vs curated 50.0 (Sonnet).
agent_test: Compare a distilled class summary, a few retrieved cases, and both, at equal tokens, and vary stored cases from 5 to 500 to look for a crossover.

claim: Rule-based versus information-integration dissociations (feedback delay, working-memory load) are a human finding with at least 25 reported cases; a neural exemplar model can mimic GCM (R^2 .981-.999). Whether the dissociations need separate systems is disputed.
agent_test: Low priority; the neural-implementation debate does not change agent design.

claim: Response times in small-N, rule-instructed designs favour serial self-terminating logical-rule models over exemplar models (EBRW poor fit), but designs were chosen to favour rules.
agent_test: Limited; no direct agent analogue.

claim: Rule use depends on working memory and age (N=113 Lewandowsky 2011; N=279 Hoffmann et al. 2014; older adults Badham 2017); effect sizes unread.
agent_test: Shrinking context may push the agent towards exemplar use; check at equal tokens. Numbers not verified.

claim: Deep CNNs replicate the Posner-Keele prototype effect: errors to criterion human 37.5, AlexNet 34.72, DenseNet-121 9.59, ResNet-18 6.52. Conference abstract only.
agent_test: None for the language agent.

claim: Shepard, Hovland and Jenkins (1961) classic order I < II < III,IV,V < VI holds for adults on separable stimuli (Nosofsky 1994). A second order, I < IV < III < V < II < VI, holds for integral stimuli, children and monkeys (Smith, Minda & Washburn 2004 are the monkey study per Pape 2015); an earlier line here that Smith et al. 2004 replicated the classic order was wrong or at least mislabelled. Rouder and Ratcliff (2004): rule model fit better with confusable stimuli, exemplar model with few distinct stimuli (abstract read; fit numbers unread).
agent_test: Build the six-type bank as an S0 calibration suite; verify the original order first.

claim: Active concept learning with LLMs: proposal-sampling strategies differ in quality; no quantified claim retained.
agent_test: Skip until numbers are read.

claim: Stated rules help only when correct. Liu et al. 2024: GPT-4-turbo 30% to 96% on linear functions with the true instruction; GPT-3.5 hypothesis accuracy vs ICL success correlation 0.0013; Kalamang grammar features 27.78% (GPT-3.5) and 22.22% (GPT-4-turbo) correct.
agent_test: Rule-then-test step: require an actual held-out check of the stated rule before it replaces the examples; compare with few-shot at equal tokens on rule and non-rule problem classes.

claim: Rule-based and example-based prompts use different, partly overlapping mechanisms in small open models (function vectors; instruction FVs lift zero-shot accuracy from under 20% to over 50%; they fail to match demonstration FVs in 10-shot). Mechanism evidence only; no behavioural equal-token effect.
agent_test: Offer both rule and example at S0 rather than one; no evidence yet that combining beats rules alone (Fu 2026: no consistent additive gain).

claim: For repeated problem types, distilled memory beats stored cases and more stored cases hurt: ReasoningBank 48.8 vs 42.1 raw trajectories; 1 retrieved experience 49.7, 4 give 44.4; AWM 45.1 vs MindAct 36.2 (gpt-4); Dynamic Cheatsheet AIME full history 26.7 vs curated 50.0. No crossover where stored cases win was found at small case counts.
agent_test: S0 memory should be a distilled class summary plus at most a few retrieved cases. Open: test with hundreds of cases.

claim: With very many in-context cases, a frontier model behaves like a nearest-neighbour (exemplar) learner: Gemini 1.5 Pro on linear classification tracks k-NN (k=5) up to 2048 shots per class, with a slight drop beyond 512 in higher dimensions.
agent_test: Predicts that a long context of stored cases pushes the agent toward exemplar-style behaviour, the opposite of the human working-memory effect. Untested on category structures.

claim: Founding-study numbers remain unread for Rouder and Ratcliff 2004 (body), Rouder and Ratcliff 2006, Goodman et al. 2008, Smith and Minda 2000, Nosofsky 2000, Feldman 2000, Lewandowsky 2011, Hoffmann et al. 2014. Only abstracts or search summaries were seen; paywalls, bot walls and 404s blocked the full texts, and arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs were rate-limited this run.
agent_test: Treat all founding-study claims as qualitative until a human with library access supplies the PDFs.
